article_title: Incorporating Early Learning Strategies in the School Improvement Grants (SIG) Program: How Three Schools Integrated Early Childhood Strategies into School Turnaround Efforts to Improve Instruction for All Students
citation: Connors-Tadros, L., Dunn, L., Martella, J., & McCauley, C. (2015). Incorporating early learning strategies in the School Improvement Grants (SIG) program: How three schools integrated early childhood strategies into school turnaround efforts to improve instruction for all students. New Brunswick, NJ: National Institute for Early Education Research. https://www.nieer.org
title: Boston Public Schools early learning strategy: uniform early math and literacy curricula, teacher training, coaches, and NAEYC accreditation support
description: Boston Public Schools enlists early childhood programming in its achievement acceleration agenda by "implementing uniform mathematics and literacy programs across early learning programs and including teacher training and coaches." Under early childhood director Jason Sachs, BPS expanded full-day kindergarten to every five year old, moved 35 schools toward NAEYC accreditation, and supported Orchard Gardens, which attained accreditation for its preschool and kindergarten classrooms in 2011 with the highest scores in the district. Internal and independent studies reveal positive effects on student performance in both the short and long terms.
requirements: District investment in uniform standards and curricula in math and literacy, expanded teacher training, and use of instructional coaches
constraints: The yearlong NAEYC accreditation process is described as rigorous and intensive
target_learners: Four-year-old preschoolers and kindergartners in a large urban district, including English language learners and students with disabilities
target_learning_goals: Improved early literacy and mathematics learning supporting short- and long-term achievement
examples: Orchard Gardens revitalized its K0–K2 curricula and implemented new reading and math frameworks school-wide with BPS early childhood supports
key_sources: Connors-Tadros, L., Dunn, L., Martella, J., & McCauley, C. (2015). Incorporating early learning strategies in the School Improvement Grants (SIG) program: How three schools integrated early childhood strategies into school turnaround efforts to improve instruction for all students. New Brunswick, NJ: National Institute for Early Education Research. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED562080

article_title: Developing a best practice framework for clinical competency education in the traditional East-Asian medicine curriculum.
citation: Han Sang Yun, Lee Seung-Hee, Chae Han. (2022). Developing a best practice framework for clinical competency education in the traditional East-Asian medicine curriculum. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03398-4
title: A five-step Best Practice Framework for reviewing and establishing clinical competency education
description: The article develops a Best Practice Framework (BPF) that structures the description of a clinical competency education system in five steps: "governance of the educational system, competency of the graduates, educational resources, assessment strategies and tools, and gaps in the curriculum". Each step yields a reviewable component of the system, from organizational governance through curriculum gaps. The authors state the framework "has not been reported previously" and offer it as a reference for countries and colleges building or upgrading traditional medicine clinical education.
requirements: A governance body in charge of the overall educational system, adequate teaching, assessment strategies, and resources must be prepared to implement competency-based education
constraints: The study notes the program reviewed "would be the first step in developing a BPF", indicating the framework is a preliminary model pending stakeholder perspectives and educational outcomes
target_learners: undergraduate students of traditional East-Asian medicine
target_learning_goals: clinical competency in skills, procedures, diagnosis and patient communication
examples: The framework was applied to Pusan National University School of Korean Medicine, whose system was "systematically described through 5 steps of governance"
key_sources: Han Sang Yun, Lee Seung-Hee, Chae Han. (2022). Developing a best practice framework for clinical competency education in the traditional East-Asian medicine curriculum. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03398-4
